title: Kaiya Dragonsister
dek: A reserved intelligence operative who turns toward ancestry research after a near-fatal experience, tests stories against evidence and makes room for quiet companionship.

facts.Personal account: Connects her turn toward study with nearly dying
facts.Library meeting: Meets Eldin; research hypotheses remain unproved

sources: Zarathis_Dragonsisters_NPC_Master.md — supplied 5 October 2026; quest-RP parts 024, 026, 030 and explicit evidence distinctions
body:
Kaiya is one of the Dragonsisters, but public recognition does not turn her into a comfortable public figure. Patient, cautious and increasingly absorbed in study, she brings the habits of an operative to questions about her own people. Her library meeting with Eldin reveals humor, skepticism and a personal reason for choosing knowledge.

A reluctant place in the spotlight

Captain Zythienne introduces her as Kaiyah at the celebration on 15, Month of Cala, Year 2. Later scenes use Kaiya. Both names belong to the same established Dragonsister.

She hides shyly as the three sisters are honored for approximately five years of service among the enemy. The narrator confirms their closeness and names Sheeva as their social leader. Kaiya’s quieter presence is not an absence of contribution.

When Eldin later asks to hear her story, she says it was a story of service out of sight and wonders how much brighter the sisters can shine after their moment of recognition. The answer is modest, but it also leaves room for a life that need not keep repeating the ceremony.

Guile and tact

Kaiya tells Eldin she is of the Veil and that combat is not for her. She prefers guile and tact. Her account places careful, indirect work beside the courage publicly attributed to the sisters.

She describes herself as more patient or cautious than Sheeva, but acknowledges Eldin’s persistence and kindness. Reserve is a matter of pace and trust; she still accepts the dance and makes her own invitations.

Her precise office and full institutional standing remain unresolved. Sheeva’s compatible account of a household raised on Emerald Veil principles gives context, without turning either sister’s words into a complete membership register.

The library date becomes a real conversation

After the war, Kaiya chooses passion studies while Minyah goes back toward fieldwork. She wants to discover how Dragonborn first came to be and how far their ancestry can be traced through an incomplete record. Eldin offers tales from another land, and she proposes the library over strong tea.

The later meeting actually occurs. Eldin finds her with a gold-and-red book about draconic blood, and she invites him to sit while asking him to keep his voice low. Libraries are sacred spaces to her.

She considers whether Dragonborn might descend from a hybrid lineage, including a possible Yuan-ti connection. It remains her hypothesis. She questions what a dragon’s assumed human form would mean for ancestry and asks where reliable evidence can be found, separating old tales from rigorously recorded research.

She is also capable of a quiet joke. When Eldin mistakes the red ink for actual dragon blood, she corrects him with shy laughter. Her plan is to read everything available before moving on, perhaps with an adventure story in between. Meticulousness and curiosity make the study a chosen life, not merely a list of unanswered lore questions.

What the mask remembers

Asked whether she has always been the bookish sister, Kaiya says she was not, until she nearly tasted death. She points to her mask. The change toward study is connected to a near-fatal experience in her own account, not an invented medical history.

She is less willing to accept every frightening story as fact. When Eldin brings up Death, she knows the warning against bringing people back, yet calls the figure a tale told to children. Reports of direct encounters are difficult for her to believe, and she asks to hear from a witness.

Her skepticism records what she believes at that moment. It does not undo the company’s quest-established encounters with Death. Nor does it settle how much she learns later, or identify the exact wound and circumstances beneath her mask.

A sister who watches how people are treated

Kaiya approves of Eugene because he is humble and treats Sheeva with dignity. She judges the relationship through his conduct toward someone she loves, rather than his public stature. Her role is that of an observing sister, distinct from Sheeva’s romance.

She tells Eldin that Sheeva is the gregarious one and apologizes for her own shyness in crowds. Their library conversation ends because she has a meditation class to attend. She can enjoy his company and still keep a commitment of her own.

The library invitation becomes a meeting, but neither scene establishes marriage, a permanent partnership or a shared household. Her sisters’ different choices leave her free to pursue knowledge without abandoning the family that made those choices possible.

The open record

Kaiya’s age, confirmed ancestry, full Veil office, completed research findings and later fate remain unresolved. Her near-death experience is her own account; it is not a recovered description of a battle or proof of how either sister received an apparent scar.

What is visible is a change in what she finds worth doing: after hidden service and danger, she chooses a patient search, asks hard questions about evidence and lets another person share a quiet table. No origin theory is declared true simply because it interests her.
